resources.string: Only watches Instagram and YouTube, to detect when Reels or Shorts are opened and send you back out of them. When a Reel is opened from a DM, it reads the chat name so Reels sent in chats you allow can play. Other apps’ screens are never read (only which app is in front), no messages are read, and the app has no internet access, so nothing ever leaves your phone.
You asked Snoozy to keep them asleep, so you’ve been sent back.
Snoozy needs Android’s Accessibility permission to spot Reels and Shorts. Before you decide, we’ll show you exactly what it can see.

Snoozy uses Android’s AccessibilityService API to block Reels and Shorts. It can’t work without it.

What it sees: only the Instagram and YouTube apps. It checks what’s on screen in those apps to tell when Reels or Shorts open. When a Reel is opened from an Instagram DM, it reads that chat’s name so Reels from chats you allow can play.

What it does: while snoozing, it closes Reels and Shorts by going back, mutes their sound, and shows a short message.

What it never does: it doesn’t read other apps, your messages or anything you type. Chat names are stored only on your phone. Snoozy has no internet access, so no data is collected, shared or sold.

Android will warn that Snoozy gets “full control”. It shows that warning for every accessibility app. You can turn Snoozy off at any time in Settings > Accessibility.
